findings.title: float: right on a flex item is ignored after making .small-action a flex container
findings.body: .small-action is now `display: flex` (line 264), so `float` on its direct children has no effect. The `button { float: right; }` rule (line 309) and `clear: both` (line 312) are now dead, meaning the small-action action button will no longer be pushed to the right edge but will sit immediately after the description. Use `margin-left: auto` on the button instead (as was done for .d-header .panel).

findings.title: order(3) on .panel without explicit order on siblings relies on default order 0
findings.body: .d-header .panel gets `@include order(3)` while .title has no order and .extra-info-wrapper (topic.scss) gets order(2). For the legacy `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` prefix the initial value is 1, not 0, so under old WebKit the un-ordered .title (group 1) and the explicitly ordered items still work, but any sibling relying on default ordering is fragile; also `order(3)` is redundant given `margin-left: auto` already pushes .panel right. Consider setting explicit orders on all header flex children or dropping the order include.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits invalid values for legacy prefixes
findings.body: The mixin blindly forwards the argument to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, which only accept start/end/center/baseline/stretch. Calling `align-items(flex-start)` or `align-items(flex-end)` (likely in future use) emits invalid declarations for those legacy properties, silently losing alignment in old WebKit/IE10. Either map values or drop the obsolete box-model prefixes.

findings.title: .d-header .contents previously relied on floats for layout; floated non-flex descendants may need review
findings.body: Converting .contents to flex removes the effect of float on its direct children (the old `.title { float: left }` and `.panel { float: right }` were deleted). `.icons`/`.login-button` still use `float: left` but are inside .panel, which is not a flex container, so they still work; however there is no `flex-wrap`/`min-width: 0` on the flex items, so long titles can overflow instead of shrinking as they did with the float layout. Worth verifying narrow-viewport header rendering.
